root_cause.text: hfs_bnode_create() returns an existing hashed node without incrementing its reference count, causing a reference count mismatch that later triggers a kernel panic when the node is freed.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states "it currently returns the existing node without incrementing its reference count" leading to "kernel BUG at fs/hfsplus/bnode.c:676! BUG_ON(!atomic_read(&node->refcnt))". The patch fixes this by returning ERR_PTR(-EEXIST) instead of the node.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix hfs_bnode_create to return -EEXIST when node already exists instead of returning the existing node, preventing potential misuse.
intent_record.what: Changed the return value in hfs_bnode_create from returning the existing node pointer to returning ERR_PTR(-EEXIST) when a node with the given number is already hashed.
intent_record.how: Callers will now receive an error pointer instead of a valid node pointer when the node already exists, allowing proper error handling instead of silently using an already-existing node.
